head: 9e887fecb04960f6d16ad69f9a2a5c31cd40157e
phase: P29 - Source closure complete; production externally blocked
method: Semantic subject-to-module mapping validated against a production import-reachability graph, executed tests separated from source-text assertions, and executed gate results. Source-text assertions are graded SOURCE COMPLETE, never UNIT TESTED.

requirements.subject: Local-first governed product definition — OCADE remains a local-first, permission-governed operating layer spanning Chat, Logic, Copilot/Cowork, browser, desktop, mobile, voice, research, code workspaces, application learning, security, evidence, recovery, packaging, and operations without hiding where processing occurs.

Live repository and retained evidence are authoritative — Every completion claim is verified against the live repository, executable tests, build output, runtime observations, checkpoints, handoffs, and retained evidence; documentation alone is insufficient.
requirements.evidence: 773 paths committed in 10 reviewable path-scoped commits and pushed; remote HEAD b3ed79d matches local exactly; retained evidence in release/ regenerated from executed output

requirements.subject: Evidence ladder and honest status classification — Every requirement uses the defined evidence classes and never conflates source existence, tests, simulation, real runtime, external blockers, or production readiness.
Historical baseline must be revalidated — Historical percentages, test counts, branch data, and HEAD values may be carried forward only after current command output independently confirms them.
requirements.evidence: historical 3,474-test and 24-gate claims revalidated against current output and corrected

requirements.subject: Original-core and expanded-programme scopes remain separate — Completion is recalculated separately for the original core and the expanded marketplace, enterprise, telemetry, bounty, public-proof, release, and hardware-elimination scope.

Mandatory requirement-to-code traceability — The audit produces exact counts, owners, files, tests, commands, dependencies, defects, evidence, acceptance tests, and a dependency-ordered execution roadmap.

Non-destructive repository preservation — Planning and audit work does not reset, clean, stash, discard, switch worktrees, delete untracked work, mass-format, commit, push, merge, rebase, apply live migrations, modify real credentials, sign, publish, or deploy without approval.
requirements.evidence: no reset, clean, stash, force-push, merge or rebase; full worktree backup taken before any change; fast-forward push only, after owner approval

requirements.subject: Universal governed loop and control hierarchy — Consequential work follows observe, understand, plan, validate, risk, permission, deterministic execution, independent verification, receipt, recovery, and trusted continuation while preferring API, plug-in, CLI, file, DOM, accessibility, native, vision, then scoped input.

Systematic hardware and tooling blocker reduction — A blocker is genuinely external only after portable runtimes, hosted runners, emulators, free equivalents, existing devices, authorised remote workers, peer-to-peer paths, signed external evidence, community skills, and one-step human actions have been evaluated.
requirements.evidence: src/lib/blocker-resolution.ts, the reachable admin launch-gate policy panel, release/OCADE_BLOCKER_REDUCTION_POLICY.json and src/lib/__tests__/blocker-resolution.test.ts enforce all ten alternatives in order, fresh digest-bound independent evidence, available-route preference, one explicit lawful owner action, cancellation, tenant-scoped retention and idempotency across 13 executed tests.
requirements.caveat: The evaluator proves the classification workflow; each live release blocker still needs its own current ten-route assessment and real owner evidence before that individual blocker can be called external.

requirements.subject: Validation, readiness, and handoff contract — Every change passes focused and full validation, production readiness requires real target evidence and operations, and every handoff records exact repository state, tests, blockers, next file, next command, expected output, and required approvals.
Provider-neutral build-runner abstraction
requirements.evidence: The tracked portable release manifest translates the same bounded jobs to hosted, self-hosted and alternate-cloud providers; the executed test rejects provider, command, secret and path drift.

requirements.subject: Hermetic portable toolchain capsule
requirements.evidence: The portable release gate enforces exact Node, npm, Rust and TypeScript versions, explicit lockfiles, environment allowlisting and toolchain-first PATH policy; complete Vitest passed.

requirements.subject: Reproducible native artifact verification
requirements.evidence: Independent provenance tests compare source, compiler, dependency digests, flags, symbols and artifact hashes, distinguish exact from normalized equivalence, and reject deliberate drift.

requirements.subject: Prebuilt sidecar and runtime bundle strategy
requirements.evidence: Sidecar selection requires target identity, HTTPS, version, rollback and matching SHA-256; missing published bundles and tampered bytes fail closed, while actual publication remains external.

requirements.subject: Clean-machine snapshot matrix
requirements.evidence: The clean-machine contract covers Windows, Linux, Android and macOS lifecycle receipts and refuses repository, developer-tool, credential, leftover, missing-step and retained-environment contamination.

requirements.subject: Remote hardware evidence network
requirements.evidence: Signed plan and tester-attestation envelopes bind the exact source, target version, app, device and benchmark; forged, stale, duplicate, privacy-leaking and impossible-hardware receipts are refused. An actual independent tester remains external.

requirements.subject: Virtual audio, microphone, camera, and clipboard laboratory
requirements.evidence: A production-owned CI/disposable-VM media-lab contract now provides five scoped virtual adapters and twelve deterministic fixtures. Executed tests cover exact consumption/emission digests, absence, denial, unplug, silence, noise, long streams, malformed frames, protected speech, cancellation, tenant and permission refusal, bounded resources, recovery and false real-hardware claims.
requirements.caveat: This is simulated media-lab evidence only. Acoustic quality, driver differences and physical camera behaviour still require real-device proof.

requirements.subject: Headless accessibility-tree simulator
requirements.evidence: release/OCADE_A11Y_SIMULATOR_EVIDENCE.json — 13/13 adversarial scenarios executed against the governed HandExecutor/EyeObserver contract
requirements.caveat: Simulator only. No real application, accessibility API or operating system involved.

requirements.subject: Application digital-twin laboratory
requirements.evidence: release/OCADE_TWIN_LAB_EVIDENCE.json — 17/17 across nine adversarial twins; route selection, unsafe-downgrade refusal, ground-truth verification, interruption, cancellation, emergency stop and verified rollback
requirements.caveat: Twin only. No licensed application, real GUI toolkit, display or input device involved. Real application support remains unproven.

requirements.subject: Open-source application equivalence programme
requirements.evidence: The production-owned substitution fabric maps six brand-neutral capability/format categories to FreeCAD, Blender, CalculiX, LibreOffice, GIMP and Audacity reference adapters and refuses unsupported capability or format pairs. Receipts remain CATEGORY CAPABILITY EVIDENCE ONLY and explicitly deny commercial-application support.
requirements.caveat: Installed free-tool execution and every commercial application/version still require independent runtime evidence.

requirements.subject: Remote licensed-worker adapter
requirements.evidence: Signed worker, job and evidence envelopes now bind tenant, user, application/version, capability and input/output digests. Tests refuse revocation, offline state, exported licence secrets, expiry, protected files, excessive retry, cancellation, capability drift and evidence mismatch.
requirements.caveat: No licensed application or authorised remote workstation was connected; receipts remain execution candidates requiring real evidence.

requirements.subject: Browser-first functional substitution layer
requirements.evidence: The substitution registry records the original request and actual route, requires explicit off-device consent plus provider, privacy and pricing disclosures, preserves output-format contracts, honours stop/revocation and never claims the requested desktop application was used.
requirements.caveat: No third-party browser provider, account, pricing tier or live data transfer was exercised.

requirements.subject: WebAssembly execution fallback
requirements.evidence: A real deterministic WebAssembly module executes twice through a typed runner contract that binds package digest, tenant, capability, memory, time, file and network limits. Tampering, over-limit execution, nondeterminism, network attempts, undeclared files, cancellation and emergency stop fail closed.
requirements.caveat: The evidence is bounded unit execution; large GPU work and operating-system control are explicitly not replaced.

requirements.subject: WebGPU and CPU tiered local inference
requirements.evidence: The local inference ladder now selects WebGPU, native GPU, vector CPU or micro CPU from measured memory, GPU memory, driver, thermal and model-compatibility constraints and records every fallback reason plus truthful latency/context/privacy metadata.
requirements.caveat: No local model was downloaded or executed on WebGPU/native GPU in this environment; route selection still requires runtime inference evidence.

requirements.subject: Progressive model download and micro-model bootstrap
requirements.evidence: Signed model manifests now support bootstrap-first compatibility and storage checks, resumable digest-bound chunks, idempotent resume, corruption/incomplete-package refusal, final package verification, rollback metadata and garbage collection that preserves bootstrap, active and rollback models.
requirements.caveat: No distributable model package or network download was supplied; verified package state does not claim model execution.

requirements.subject: Encrypted burst-compute provider
requirements.evidence: Burst policy requires approved providers, fresh explicit consent, non-protected minimum transformed payloads, retention/pricing disclosure, bounded retries and local fallback. Tests execute AES-256-GCM sealing with tenant/job/provider associated-data binding and refuse tampering, stale consent, outage, partial results and retention/evidence drift.
requirements.caveat: No remote provider was contacted and no cost was incurred; signed results remain provider-runtime candidates.

requirements.subject: Home-node and spare-device compute mesh
requirements.evidence: Signed measured-node attestations and scoped jobs now bind tenant, user, certificate identity, capability and input digest over approved LAN mutual-TLS or E2E peer transports. Tests refuse revocation, offline/expired nodes, impossible claims, public addresses, duplicates, capability drift, protected data and excessive retries while allowing private IP changes without identity drift.
requirements.caveat: No spare physical device or live peer transport was connected.

requirements.subject: Browser extension zero-touch test profile
requirements.evidence: src/lib/__tests__/extension-zero-touch.test.ts - 14 tests EXECUTING extension/background.js in a VM with a recording chrome double; protocol rejection, pairing enforcement, no-API-touch-while-unpaired, manifest minimality
requirements.caveat: The chrome API is a double. No real tab, DOM or permission prompt. Proves the extension's decisions, NOT that it works in Chrome; scripting.executeScript reaching a page is unproven until the extension is loaded for real.

requirements.subject: Enterprise browser policy deployment
requirements.evidence: The production-owned generator emits signed Chrome/Edge policies for Windows, macOS and Linux with exact tenant/package/version binding, HTTPS allow-listed update URLs, least-privilege production origins, forbidden permissions, incognito refusal, rollback and blocked-install revocation bundles. Tests reject wildcard/dev origins, unsupported combinations, tampering, expiry, replay and tenant/package drift.
requirements.caveat: Bundles explicitly report appliedToDeviceManagement=false. An organisation must approve and deploy them through its own device-management system or manual policy process.

requirements.subject: Hosted macOS and iOS simulator lane
Remote physical-device proof broker
requirements.evidence: The compatibility broker verifies signed plans and attestations against exact build, application, physical-device and benchmark bindings, then retains REAL TARGET CANDIDATE - INDEPENDENT REVIEW REQUIRED rather than self-promoting evidence.

requirements.subject: LAN-only private mode
requirements.evidence: LAN-only authorization requires QR/short-code proof, mutual local-certificate authentication, pinned fingerprints, an explicit LAN ONLY indicator, fresh authentication after subnet changes and local emergency stop. Tests accept only private IPv4/IPv6 destinations and refuse DNS queries, relays, public/hostname destinations, rogue certificates and stale pairing.
requirements.caveat: The policy is unit tested; a real packet capture proving zero external traffic remains required.

requirements.subject: Synthetic payment-provider twin
requirements.evidence: src/lib/__tests__/payments.test.ts - 30 tests executing the provider contract, HWE-29 twin and entitlement machine: forged signature, tampered payload, replay window, duplicate delivery, seen-set poisoning, out-of-order events, grace non-extension, cancellation, refund, dispute lifecycle
requirements.caveat: Synthetic provider only. No money can move: LIVE_PAYMENTS_ENABLED is a compile-time false and checkoutAllowed refuses any non-simulated provider. Live activation needs legal identity, bank verification and owner approval.

requirements.subject: Local database and identity digital twin
requirements.evidence: src/lib/__tests__/db-twin.test.ts - 14 tests executing 31 migrations against real PostgreSQL 18.3 (PGlite) with unmodified pgcrypto/pg_trgm; RLS proven to bite under SET ROLE authenticated; cross-tenant read, forged insert and anonymous access all refused
requirements.caveat: Local twin only. Not the production database: no GoTrue, realtime or storage service, and no deployment proven. Migration 20260721153321 FAILS - it comments on ficia_time_entries which no migration creates, so this set cannot rebuild the database from scratch.

requirements.subject: Local secrets broker and credential-presence wizard
requirements.evidence: release/OCADE_TRUST_SETUP_POLICY.json, scripts/trust-setup.mjs and src/lib/__tests__/trust-setup.test.ts - 15 tests verify presence-only inspection, exact setup destinations, scoped one-call credential injection, consumer/project/scope/revocation refusal, secret-free audit receipts, rotation, removal and cancellation.
requirements.caveat: The broker contract is unit tested with an injected secure-store adapter. Real Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain and Linux Secret Service integration plus production credential entry remain external owner/runtime work.

requirements.subject: Self-signed trust laboratory
requirements.evidence: release/OCADE_P26_UPDATE_TRUST_EVIDENCE.json, src/lib/packaging/update-trust.ts and src/lib/__tests__/update-trust.test.ts - 17 executed Ed25519 trust-lab tests cover canonical manifests, tampering, wrong keys, unsigned artifacts, expiry, rotation, revocation, downgrade, rollback and placeholder-key refusal.
requirements.caveat: This is an explicit test-only trust laboratory. It is not a production certificate, public trust chain, signed installer or notarized release.

requirements.subject: Open-source signing eligibility path
requirements.evidence: release/OCADE_TRUST_SETUP_POLICY.json, scripts/trust-setup.mjs and src/lib/__tests__/trust-setup.test.ts validate public-source, SPDX-licence, owner-approval, reproducibility, notice and proprietary-input eligibility rules and reject product-code/community-signing conflation.
requirements.caveat: No current component is eligible: candidate component licences and public repositories require owner/legal publication decisions, and the proprietary OCADE product is explicitly prohibited from community open-source signing routes.

requirements.subject: Application-skill marketplace as a hardware multiplier
requirements.evidence: src/lib/skills/marketplace.ts integrates the existing real-Ed25519 skill-trust evaluator with independent review, reputation, sandbox, version binding, local revalidation, digest-bound acceptance evidence, tenant-scoped persistence and durable revocation. src/lib/__tests__/marketplace-bounty.test.ts exercises the reachable Settings UI boundary and registry flow within a 21-test marketplace/bounty suite.
requirements.caveat: The marketplace is local review and installation only. No hosted catalogue, external contributor, target-application licence or real community publication has been proven, and simulated admission never claims the target application ran.

requirements.subject: Community compatibility bounty engine
requirements.evidence: src/lib/skills/marketplace.ts and src/lib/__tests__/marketplace-bounty.test.ts cover bounded priority requests, duplicate claims, requester self-claim refusal, claimant identity, version mismatch, fraudulent/partial/simulated evidence, exact acceptance criteria, independent review, disputes, later revocation and tenant isolation.
requirements.caveat: This is a non-financial priority-credit engine. Escrow, identity verification and payouts remain externally blocked until compliant payment infrastructure and contributor identity checks exist.

requirements.subject: Opt-in failure telemetry and hardware-gap prioritisation
requirements.evidence: src/lib/__tests__/failure-telemetry.test.ts - 18 tests: consent-off default, consent withdrawal discarding the queue, allow-list dropping window titles/clipboard/email/home paths, redaction of paths/emails/tokens/JWTs/IPs inside allowed fields, bounded queue, user-readable payload
requirements.caveat: No transmission endpoint exists; reports are queued locally only. Nothing has ever been sent.

requirements.subject: Synthetic fault and chaos hardware injector
requirements.evidence: Nine policy-declared fault cases are restricted to explicit test shims and require checkpointing, one bounded retry, a user-visible reason, rollback and unique mutation identifiers. Results remain labelled SIMULATED FAULT ONLY.

requirements.subject: Deterministic replay of real control sessions
One-click environment doctor and repair engine
Automatic provider substitution with transparent receipts
requirements.evidence: P21 production wiring: module now reachable from a route/server function. Verified by import-graph reachability (test-only modules 10 -> 0) and by the integration honesty gate (nonRuntimeModules 5 -> 0).

requirements.subject: Evidence-weighted completion engine
requirements.evidence: scripts/readiness-engine.mjs recalculates all 510 unique rows and per-area dimensions; seven Phase 29 tests, including deliberate score inflation, passed in the complete Vitest suite.

requirements.subject: Automatic stale-evidence invalidation
requirements.evidence: The P29 engine invalidates future, expired, source-revision-drifted and target-version-drifted evidence; the focused cases passed inside the complete Vitest suite.

requirements.subject: Privacy-preserving screenshot and UI evidence redaction
requirements.evidence: Evidence intake requires pre-capture masking, redacts protected values, payment data, OTPs and paths locally, stores only the original digest, refuses unmasked screenshots and downgrades excessively redacted evidence to LOCALLY VERIFIED ONLY. No real screenshot was uploaded.

requirements.subject: User-owned compatibility lab mode
requirements.evidence: Compatibility-lab authorisation is local-first and requires low-risk rehearsed actions, explicit permissions, a bounded action budget, cancellation and separate publication consent.

requirements.subject: Remote support session without unrestricted access
requirements.evidence: Support sessions expose diagnostics and plans only, bind identity and expiry, support revocation and emergency stop, refuse protected content and direct control, and require local approval for mutations.

requirements.subject: Portable compatibility pack export
requirements.evidence: The offline compatibility pack is signed and binds tenant, platform, component versions, licences, digests, expiry and rollback metadata; tampering is rejected.

requirements.subject: Air-gapped local update and evidence workflow
requirements.evidence: Signed offline pack verification refuses replay, downgrade, tampering and tenant mismatch and preserves rollback data. A physical removable-media run remains external.

requirements.subject: interviews
requirements.evidence: release/OCADE_STAKEHOLDER_RESEARCH_POLICY.json, src/lib/stakeholder-research.ts, the admin launch-gate research boundary and 17 executed stakeholder-research tests provide a consented, pseudonymous, independently reviewed, tenant-scoped intake contract that excludes synthetic fixtures from production evidence.
requirements.caveat: Zero production participants are recorded. The product-research owner must recruit consenting external humans and conduct real interviews.

requirements.subject: workflow observation
requirements.evidence: The stakeholder-research intake requires explicit observation authorisation, withdrawal support, digest-bound evidence, independent review, current timestamps and no raw or protected content retention.
requirements.caveat: No authorised human workflow has been observed. The research owner and participant must schedule and consent to real observation.

requirements.subject: pain points
requirements.evidence: The evidence contract accepts pain-point findings only from current external-human records with consent, privacy, coverage and independent-review proof; synthetic fixtures are excluded by the production assessment.
requirements.caveat: No real participant pain-point evidence exists. Human discovery is owner-coordinated external work.

requirements.subject: task frequency
requirements.evidence: The research programme gate requires five distinct current external participants per dimension and rejects duplicated pseudonyms or synthetic task-frequency records.
requirements.caveat: No real task-frequency sample has been collected. Participant recruitment and observation remain external.

requirements.subject: risk mapping
requirements.evidence: Risk-mapping evidence is governed by the same current, consented, pseudonymous, independently reviewed and tenant-scoped contract, with raw/protected participant content prohibited.
requirements.caveat: No stakeholder-validated risk map has been observed. External participants and the accountable research owner are required.

requirements.subject: accessibility
requirements.area: Stakeholder Discovery and Workflow Research; GUI Integration and No-Dead-Control Enforcement
requirements.evidence: The research contract includes accessibility as a mandatory distinct coverage dimension and proves that duplicate or synthetic participants cannot satisfy its minimum; repository accessibility gates remain separate technical evidence.
requirements.caveat: No research sessions with real users of assistive technology are recorded. Accessibility stakeholder validation requires consenting external participants.

requirements.subject: regional needs
requirements.evidence: Regional-needs coverage uses non-identifying coverage tags, current external-human evidence, independent review and minimum distinct-participant gates while rejecting email, phone and URL-shaped identifiers.
requirements.caveat: No real regional stakeholder sample is recorded. Recruitment across intended regions remains an owner-led external action.
